# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Fill this in as you work. It is the human-readable record of HOW this iteration was done and is snapshotted with the candidate, so anyone — and the next iteration via ./prior_iterations/ — can see your reasoning. Be concrete.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula written instead of literal value (grader reads data_only, no recalc → None) | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 37456, 53647, 54144, 55979, 56563, 9569 (+ partly 80-42) | agent follows "create a formula" literally; nothing told it the grader never recalculates | KNOWLEDGE | output contract + rewrite-with-reason |
| 2 | B. Wasted turns / no verification | most failing traces (e.g. repeated identical code ~28× with "no output") | template said "once that file exists, you are done"; no instruction to print/verify | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure + verify step + stop rule |
| 3 | C. Pattern misread vs pre-filled examples / wrong header row | 39046, 43436, 48527, 59196, 50768, 51-12 | agent computed without checking it reproduces pre-filled answer cells / expected-result blocks; assumed header=row 1 | BEHAVIORAL | procedure step "examples are ground truth, reproduce before writing" |
| 4 | D. to_excel rewrites shift / destroy layout | 227-40, 48527, 50768, 80-42 | DataFrame write offsets (index i = row i+2), header omitted, sheets dropped | KNOWLEDGE | "write with openpyxl" rule + pandas offset note |
| 5 | E. Instruction semantics (fill colour, exact strings, error cells) | 267-18, 55979, 56563 | fill check on wrong attribute; reworded sheet name; #NUM! not skipped | KNOWLEDGE | practical notes |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | role/goal line + output contract (rewrite with reason) | prompt.md "How your work is graded" | explains the data_only/no-recalc grading so "formula" requests are satisfied by the computed value; type rules match transform_value | yes — no passing trace wrote formulas |
| D | add rule + knowledge | prompt.md "Writing the file" | openpyxl load/edit/save preserves sheets & coordinates; pandas index→row offset | yes — openpyxl and to_excel-in-place both still allowed for reading; passing writes were literal values |
| B, C | restructure into ordered procedure | prompt.md "Procedure" | inspect → derive rule from examples → compute & self-check against examples → write → reopen & print → no-code stop | yes — passing tasks already wrote correct values; verification only adds read-only rounds |
| E | knowledge notes | prompt.md "Practical notes" | fgColor.rgb inspection, skip error strings, exact spelling, header rows in result tables, no repeated identical code | yes — generic, no task values |
| A, B | output contract at point of use | task_template.md | all 6 required placeholders + {max_turns} kept; removed "once file exists you are done"; adds value-not-formula + verify + stop lines | yes — placeholder contract validated with str.format |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- A: 53647 wrote `=E5/E6`-style formulas → golden E7=8.75, E8=10 are literals; contract now says compute and write the literal. Same for 54144 (golden 92.5,129.94,192.32,42) and 56563 (77772.6, sum skipping #NUM! — covered by error-string note). Blast radius: 18 passing tasks all wrote literals already; no change.
- D: 227-40 to_excel wrote deduped rows without header and offset → golden A14:E17 = header + rows; openpyxl absolute-coordinate write + "include header if expected example does". Blast radius: passing to_excel users (e.g. 12864, 2768) were single-sheet value writes; openpyxl yields identical cells.
- B: traces that resubmitted identical no-output code → procedure step 5 forces a printed repr check, step 6 a no-code stop, and "never resend identical code". Blast radius: adapter gives 3 verify turns that cannot change the file once it exists unless the agent rewrites it — reread-only is safe.
- C: 39046 (golden F2:F6=2,2,0,2,2 per-row, agent wrote a total), 43436 (per-Department counts), 59196 (header in row 2, agent read row 1 → None) → step 1 'Unnamed' header hint, step 2-3 reproduce pre-filled cells before writing. Blast radius: 59595/48620/382-10/416-15/9726 changed pre-filled cells legitimately — wording says examples show the pattern, never "do not touch them".
- E: 267-18 yellow only on G2 (FFFFFF00), G1 green → note to print fgColor.rgb before filtering; 55979 golden 'Supplier_1' (sheet name) → "match the text exactly as the data spells it".

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): none — serial, the session forbids AgentTool unless requested. Diagnosed all 40 seed traces via condensed dumps and compared failing answer cells against golden workbooks with openpyxl (read-only).
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): none exist (empty seed, iteration 1/1); rejected.jsonl empty.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The "no recalculation → write literal values" contract with its reason (largest cluster).
- Placeholder contract in task_template.md (all six required + {max_turns}).
- Phrasing that pre-filled cells are *examples to reproduce*, not cells to freeze.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- 80-42 (~96k-cell multi-sheet consolidation): specific failure is scale/structure; only general levers (openpyxl write, verify) apply — no bespoke rule.
- 9569 (1280-row formula): covered by cluster A only; no task-specific hint.
- 50768 risk-matrix layout: covered by generic "examples are ground truth / exact format" rule; no matrix-specific guidance to avoid overfitting.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
